examples.ko: 두 사람이 책상을 사이에 두고 마주해서 이야기했어요.
examples.en: The two talked face to face with a desk between them.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어려운 현실을 마주하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is facing a difficult reality.
It was an evening spent face to face with my family after a long time.

examples.ko: 문제를 피하지 말고 한번 마주해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't avoid the problem; try facing it.
When I opened the door, I came face to face with a stranger.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 마주하면 말없이 웃기만 해요.
examples.en: When the two come face to face, they just smile without a word.

explain: '만나다'는 약속하고 보는 것이고, '마주하다'는 얼굴이나 상황을 정면으로 대하는 느낌이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 '현실을 마주하다', '문제를 마주하다'처럼 피하고 싶은 일에도 써요. '마주 앉다', '마주 보다'는 띄어 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: '만나다' is meeting by arrangement, while '마주하다' has the feel of facing a person or situation head-on. It is used not only for people but also for things you would rather avoid, as in '현실을 마주하다' (face reality). '마주 앉다' and '마주 보다' are written with a space.

examples.en: All the survey results have been collected.

examples.ko: 여러 나라의 우표가 한곳에 수집돼 있어요.
examples.en: Stamps from many countries are collected in one place.
I'll let you know as soon as the data is collected.
The collected data is saved on the computer.
Please explain how the data is collected.
The students' opinions were gathered and taken to the meeting.

explain: '수집되다'는 모으는 사람이 아니라 모이는 자료가 주어예요. 모으는 사람을 말하려면 '수집하다'를 써요. '모이다'는 사람이 모일 때도 쓰지만 '수집되다'는 사람에게 쓰지 않고, 자료·정보·의견과 같이 써요.
explain_en: With '수집되다' the subject is the material being gathered, not the person gathering; use '수집하다' for the collector. '모이다' can be used when people gather, but '수집되다' is not used for people and goes with data, information, and opinions.

examples.en: I fitted new tires on the car.
A drone fitted with a camera flies in the sky.

examples.ko: 휴대폰에 케이스를 장착하는 데 일 분도 안 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes less than a minute to put a case on the phone.

examples.ko: 이 의자에는 바퀴를 장착할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can attach wheels to this chair.
I mounted a light on my bike and rode at night.
Try fitting it slowly while following the manual.

explain: '달다', '끼우다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 기계·부품·장비 이야기에 어울려요. 보통 '~에 ~을 장착하다' 모양으로 써요. 게임에서 장비를 몸에 갖출 때도 '장착하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '달다' or '끼우다' and suits talk about machines, parts, and gear. It usually takes the pattern '~에 ~을 장착하다'. In games, equipping an item is also called '장착하다'.

examples.en: I'm eagerly looking forward to summer vacation.
I was looking forward to my friend coming.
I'm leaving on the trip I've long been waiting for.
I'll be hoping for good news.

examples.ko: 그 영화를 고대한 팬이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: There are so many fans who were looking forward to that movie.

examples.ko: 답장을 고대해서 매일 메일함을 열어 봐요.
examples.en: I look forward to a reply, so I check my inbox every day.

explain: '기다리다'보다 기대가 크고 격식 있는 느낌이에요. 편지나 이메일 끝에 '답장을 고대합니다'처럼 써요. 좋은 일에 쓰고, 나쁜 일을 기다릴 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It feels more eager and formal than '기다리다'. It is used at the end of letters and emails, as in '답장을 고대합니다'. It is used for good things, not for bad things you are waiting for.

examples.en: The court judged this case fairly.
Citizens judge politicians through elections.
It is hard for one person to judge another.

examples.ko: 신이 모든 사람을 심판한다고 믿는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people believe God judges everyone.
They asked for the wrongdoer to be judged.

examples.ko: 먼저 사정을 듣고 나서 심판해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to hear the circumstances first and then judge.

explain: 경기에서 심판을 볼 때는 '심판을 보다'라고 해요. '심판하다'는 잘잘못을 가려 판정을 내린다는 무거운 느낌이라 재판이나 선거 이야기에 어울려요. '판단하다', '평가하다'보다 훨씬 강하게 들려요.
explain_en: For refereeing a game, say '심판을 보다'. '심판하다' feels heavy, like weighing right and wrong and passing judgment, so it fits talk about trials and elections. It sounds much stronger than '판단하다' or '평가하다'.

examples.en: The report hasn't been submitted yet.
The documents were submitted to the school yesterday.
Once the application is submitted, a confirmation email is sent.

examples.ko: 제출된 과제는 다시 고칠 수 없어요.
examples.en: A submitted assignment can't be edited again.
Several written opinions are being submitted.

examples.ko: 모든 답안이 시간 안에 제출돼야 해요.
examples.en: All answer sheets must be submitted in time.

explain: 내는 사람이 주어이면 '제출하다', 낸 서류가 주어이면 '제출되다'를 써요. '내다'보다 공식적이라서 과제, 서류, 신청서, 보고서와 잘 어울려요. 친구에게 물건을 줄 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: When the person handing it in is the subject, use '제출하다'; when the document itself is the subject, use '제출되다'. It is more official than '내다' and goes with assignments, documents, applications, and reports. It is not used for giving a friend an item.

examples.en: The doctor diagnosed my symptoms.
The mechanic is diagnosing the cause of the breakdown.

examples.ko: 의사가 단순한 감기로 진단한 환자가 많아요.
examples.en: Many patients were diagnosed by the doctor as having just a cold.
You first have to diagnose the problem exactly.
There is a program that diagnoses the state of a computer.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 한국어 실력을 진단해 줬어요.
examples.en: My teacher assessed my Korean level for me.

explain: '진단을 받다'는 환자가, '진단하다'는 의사가 주어예요. 병뿐 아니라 기계, 회사, 실력처럼 문제를 살펴볼 때도 비유로 써요. '검사하다'는 살펴보는 일이고, '진단하다'는 결과를 보고 판단까지 내려요.
explain_en: The patient says '진단을 받다' and the doctor '진단하다'. Beyond illness, it is also used figuratively for examining machines, companies, or skills. '검사하다' is the checking itself, while '진단하다' goes on to make a judgment from the result.

examples.en: The broken bike has been repaired.
The computer gets repaired within two days.
I picked up the repaired phone today.

examples.ko: 오래된 다리가 수리되는 동안 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: While the old bridge is being repaired, the road is blocked.
I'll contact you as soon as it's repaired.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 수리되지 않아서 앉으면 위험해요.
examples.en: This chair hasn't been repaired, so it's dangerous to sit on.

explain: 고치는 사람이 주어이면 '수리하다', 고장 난 물건이 주어이면 '수리되다'예요. '고치다'는 습관이나 버릇에도 쓰지만 '수리하다'는 기계, 건물, 도로 같은 물건에만 써요.
explain_en: When the repairer is the subject use '수리하다'; when the broken item is the subject use '수리되다'. '고치다' can also be used for habits, but '수리하다' is only for things like machines, buildings, and roads.

examples.en: A new plan has been drawn up.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 안전 대책이 수립돼야 해요.
examples.en: Safety measures must be established within this year.

examples.ko: 수립된 목표를 팀원 모두가 알고 있어요.
examples.en: Every team member knows the goals that were set.
Once the rules are established, everyone has to follow them.
I studied how a new government is established.

examples.ko: 계획이 수립되지 않아서 일이 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The work is getting delayed because no plan has been made.

explain: 계획, 대책, 목표, 제도, 정부처럼 크고 공식적인 것이 세워질 때 써요. 가벼운 약속은 '정해지다'가 자연스러워요. '계획을 수립하다'와 '계획이 수립되다'는 능동과 피동으로 짝이 돼요.
explain_en: It is used when something large and official is set up: plans, measures, goals, systems, or a government. For casual arrangements, '정해지다' sounds natural. '계획을 수립하다' and '계획이 수립되다' are the active and passive pair.

examples.en: We discussed next week's schedule.
They are discussing the budget issue in the meeting.

examples.ko: 이 일은 가족과 먼저 논의해 보세요.
examples.en: Talk this over with your family first.
There is too much to discuss.
After a long discussion, we made a decision.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 따로 만나서 논의하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I'd like the two teams to meet separately and discuss it.

explain: '이야기하다'보다 격식 있고, 결정을 내리려고 의견을 나눈다는 느낌이 있어요. '~을/를 논의하다', '~와/과 논의하다'로 써요. 친구와 수다를 떨 때는 쓰지 않고, 회의·직장·학교 발표에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '이야기하다' and suggests exchanging opinions in order to reach a decision. Use '~을/를 논의하다' or '~와/과 논의하다'. It is not for chatting with friends; it fits meetings, work, and school presentations.

examples.en: Tigers hunt at night.
People in the old days hunted animals with bows.
I saw a lion hunting on television.

examples.ko: 독수리가 토끼를 사냥할 때 정말 빨라요.
examples.en: An eagle is really fast when it hunts a rabbit.
My grandfather hunted in the mountains when he was young.

examples.ko: 이 동물은 무리를 지어 사냥해서 먹이를 구해요.
examples.en: This animal hunts in a group to find food.

explain: 사람도 동물도 먹이를 잡을 때 '사냥하다'를 써요. '사냥을 가다', '사냥을 나가다'처럼 '사냥'과 다른 동사를 같이 써도 돼요. 낚시로 물고기를 잡을 때는 '낚시하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Both people and animals '사냥하다' when they catch prey. You can also use the noun with another verb, as in '사냥을 가다' or '사냥을 나가다'. Catching fish with a rod is '낚시하다'.

examples.en: The government decided to raise interest rates.

examples.ko: 이 약은 체온을 상승시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can raise body temperature.
A good ad pushed sales up.
Exercise lifts your mood.
If you raise the price, customers decrease.

examples.ko: 회사의 가치를 상승시킨 사람은 새 대표예요.
examples.en: The person who raised the company's value is the new CEO.

explain: '올리다'와 가깝지만 더 딱딱해서 뉴스, 경제, 보고서에 어울려요. 저절로 오르는 것은 '상승하다', 올리는 사람이 있으면 '상승시키다'예요. 반대말은 '하락시키다'예요.
explain_en: It is close to '올리다' but stiffer, so it suits news, economics, and reports. Something that rises by itself is '상승하다'; when someone causes the rise, use '상승시키다'. The opposite is '하락시키다'.

examples.en: I don't want to disappoint my parents.
I disappointed my friend again.
I'm worried I'll disappoint my teacher by being late.
That concert did not disappoint the fans.

examples.ko: 기대하게 해 놓고 실망시키면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't get people's hopes up and then let them down.

examples.ko: 저를 믿어 준 사람들을 실망시킨 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never let down the people who trusted me.

explain: '실망하다'는 내가 실망할 때, '실망시키다'는 내가 다른 사람을 실망하게 만들 때 써요. '부모님을 실망시키다'처럼 '을/를'로 사람을 받아요. 죄송하다고 말할 때 '실망시켜서 죄송해요'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '실망하다' is when I am disappointed; '실망시키다' is when I make someone else disappointed. The person takes '을/를', as in '부모님을 실망시키다'. When apologizing you can say '실망시켜서 죄송해요'.

examples.en: Please enter your name here.
I entered the password wrong.
If you enter a number, the result appears.
It takes time to type in the address.
Check what you entered once more.
There's no keyboard, so I can't type anything in.

explain: 컴퓨터, 휴대폰, 기계에 글자나 숫자를 넣을 때 써요. 종이에 손으로 쓸 때는 '쓰다'나 '적다'를 써요. 반대말은 '출력하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for putting letters or numbers into a computer, phone, or machine. For writing by hand on paper, use '쓰다' or '적다'. The opposite is '출력하다'.

examples.en: Everyone's opinion must be respected.
At this school, students' choices are respected.
I like an atmosphere where everyone is respected.
If promises aren't respected, trust breaks.
Children's rights must be respected too.
I felt that my thoughts were respected.

explain: '존중하다'는 내가 존중하는 것이고, '존중되다'는 의견·권리·선택이 존중받는 상태예요. '존중받다'도 비슷한데 사람이 주어일 때 자연스러워요. '저는 존중받았어요', '제 의견이 존중됐어요'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '존중하다' is what I do; '존중되다' describes opinions, rights, or choices being respected. '존중받다' is similar but more natural when a person is the subject: '저는 존중받았어요' and '제 의견이 존중됐어요'.

examples.en: Hearing your voice puts me at ease.
I felt relieved when I heard the child got home.
I felt relieved because the doctor said it's fine.

examples.ko: 옆에 친구가 있으면 안심돼서 잠이 와요.
examples.en: With a friend beside me I feel safe and get sleepy.
Hearing the rain has stopped, I feel a bit relieved.
I'm waiting for some reassuring news.

explain: '안심하다'는 내가 마음을 놓는 행동이고, '안심되다'는 어떤 일 때문에 저절로 마음이 놓이는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~니까/~어서 안심돼요'처럼 이유와 같이 말해요. 반대는 '불안하다'예요.
explain_en: '안심하다' is the act of putting your mind at rest, while '안심되다' is the feeling of being put at ease by something. It usually comes with a reason, as in '~니까/~어서 안심돼요'. The opposite is '불안하다'.

en: set someone at ease; ease someone's mind

examples.en: The mother reassured the crying child.
The doctor smiled to reassure the patient.
I want to put my worried friend at ease.
I reassured my family by phone.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 말 한마디가 사람을 안심시킬 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes one warm word can put a person at ease.
I spoke slowly in a reassuring voice.

explain: '안심하다'는 내가 마음을 놓을 때, '안심시키다'는 내가 다른 사람의 마음을 놓게 할 때 써요. '을/를'로 사람을 받아요. '달래다'는 우는 아이나 화난 사람의 기분을 풀어 줄 때 써서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: '안심하다' is when I feel at ease; '안심시키다' is when I make someone else feel at ease, with the person marked by '을/를'. '달래다' is a little different: it is for soothing a crying child or an angry person.

en: compete; take part in a match

examples.en: Our team plays in the final tomorrow.
My younger sibling entered a marathon.

examples.ko: 다리를 다쳐서 이번 경기에 출전할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I can't play in this game.
I met an athlete who competed in the Olympics.
I really want to compete this time.
The coach let me play.

explain: '참가하다'는 모임이나 행사에 두루 쓰지만 '출전하다'는 경기나 대회에 선수로 나갈 때 써요. '대회에 출전하다', '경기에 출전하다'처럼 '에'와 같이 써요. 팀이 선수를 내보낼 때는 '내보내다'를 써요.
explain_en: '참가하다' works for meetings and events in general, but '출전하다' is for going into a match or competition as a player. It takes '에', as in '대회에 출전하다'. When a team sends a player out, it uses '내보내다'.

examples.en: Our class puts on a play at the festival.
The students performed a play on stage.
As a child I played with friends by acting out plays.
I saw a stage actor up close.
We'll be performing a play at the theater from tomorrow.
Don't put on an act and pretend to be sad.

explain: 무대 위 공연뿐 아니라 일부러 꾸며서 행동하는 것도 가리켜요. '연극하지 마'는 '진짜가 아닌 척하지 마'라는 느낌이라 친한 사이에서 써요. 공연 이야기에서는 '연극을 하다'처럼 목적어를 넣어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Besides stage performance, it can mean deliberately putting on an act. '연극하지 마' feels like 'stop pretending' and is said between close people. For a stage show you can also say '연극을 하다' with the object.

en: chief director; chairman of the board of directors

examples.en: The chairman gave a congratulatory speech at the graduation.
The chairman of our school was a teacher long ago.
I made an appointment to meet the hospital chairman.
A new chairman will be chosen next month.
The staff passed on their thanks to the chairman.
The chairman's office is at the end of the third floor.

explain: 학교, 병원, 재단처럼 이사회가 있는 곳에서 쓰는 직함이에요. 회사 대표를 가리키는 '사장'과 달라요. 부를 때는 '이사장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a title used in places that have a board of directors, such as schools, hospitals, and foundations. It differs from '사장', which refers to a company head. When addressing the person, say '이사장님'.

examples.en: A large company announced the takeover of a small firm.
The takeover price was too high, so I gave up.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 인수로 직원 수가 늘었어요.
examples.en: The number of employees grew after that company's takeover.
Please sign the receipt confirmation for the baggage.
When the takeover is done, the name will change.
The two companies agreed to the takeover.

explain: '회사 인수'처럼 회사를 사서 넘겨받을 때 써요. 회사를 파는 쪽이 넘기는 일은 '매각'이라고 해요. '인수합병'은 회사를 사고 합치는 일이에요.
explain_en: It is used for buying a company and taking it over, as in '회사 인수'. When the seller hands a company over, that is called '매각'. '인수합병' means buying companies and merging them.

examples.en: That company was acquired by a large corporation.
The small shop changed its name when it was taken over.
Even after the takeover, the staff work as before.
I want to stop it from being acquired by a rival.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 작년에 다른 회사에 인수돼서 서비스가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: This app was acquired by another company last year, and its service changed.
Before it was acquired, it was running at a loss.

explain: '인수하다'는 사는 쪽, '인수되다'는 넘어가는 회사가 주어예요. 보통 '~에/에게 인수되다'로 써요. 뉴스에서 '대기업에 인수됐다'처럼 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: With '인수하다' the buyer is the subject; with '인수되다' the company being taken over is. It usually appears as '~에/에게 인수되다'. In the news you may hear '대기업에 인수됐다'.

examples.ko: 어려운 일을 끝까지 하는 모습이 존경스러워요.
examples.en: The way you see hard things through is admirable.
I met a teacher I admire.
His words and actions were admirable.

examples.ko: 아무도 안 보는데 약속을 지키니까 존경스럽네요.
examples.en: You keep your promise even when no one is watching; that's admirable.
My grandmother's life is so admirable that I bowed my head.

examples.ko: 매일 봉사하는 이웃이 존경스러울 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I find the neighbor who volunteers every day admirable.

explain: '~을 존경하다'는 대상을 '을/를'로 받지만 '~이/가 존경스럽다'는 대상이 '이/가'로 와요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라서 '존경스러워요', '존경스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 그 사람을 보고 저절로 드는 느낌을 말해요.
explain_en: '존경하다' marks its object with '을/를', but with '존경스럽다' the person admired takes '이/가'. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular, so it becomes '존경스러워요' and '존경스러운'. It describes the feeling that arises on seeing that person.

examples.en: The author created a new story.
I played a song I composed myself for my friend.
Creating pictures or poems is enjoyable.

examples.ko: 이 이야기는 실제가 아니라 창작해서 쓴 거예요.
examples.en: This story isn't real; I made it up and wrote it.
The children are creating a dance on their own.
To create, you first have to read a lot.

explain: 이미 있는 것을 따라 할 때는 '모방하다'나 '따라 하다'를 쓰고, 새로 지어낼 때는 '창작하다'를 써요. 소설·노래·춤·시처럼 예술 작품과 잘 어울려요. 만든 사람은 '창작자'라고 해요.
explain_en: For copying something that exists, use '모방하다' or '따라 하다'; for inventing something new, use '창작하다'. It fits artistic works such as novels, songs, dances, and poems. The maker is called '창작자'.

examples.en: Many people fell victim to the accident.

examples.ko: 작은 가게들이 개발 때문에 희생되고 있어요.
examples.en: Small shops are being sacrificed because of development.
We remember the people who were lost in the war.

examples.ko: 아이들이 희생되지 않도록 안전을 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: We must keep things safe so children aren't harmed.

examples.ko: 나쁜 결정 때문에 다른 사람이 희생돼서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: Others must not be sacrificed because of a bad decision.
When someone is lost, we all grieve.

explain: '희생하다'는 자기가 일부러 내놓는 것이고, '희생되다'는 어쩔 수 없이 피해를 입거나 목숨을 잃는 것이에요. 사고, 전쟁, 재난 뉴스에서 '희생자'와 같이 나와요. 가볍게 쓰지 않는 말이에요.
explain_en: '희생하다' is giving something up on purpose, while '희생되다' is suffering harm or losing one's life against one's will. It appears with '희생자' (victim) in news about accidents, war, and disasters. It is not used lightly.

examples.ko: 부모님은 우리를 위해 많은 것을 희생하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents sacrificed a lot for us.

examples.ko: 가족을 위해 시간을 희생해야 할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes you have to give up your time for your family.
Don't work at the cost of your health.

examples.ko: 친구를 구하려고 자신을 희생한 사람 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read about a person who sacrificed himself to save a friend.

examples.ko: 저는 꿈을 위해 잠을 희생하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm sacrificing sleep for my dream.
A heart that sacrifices for everyone is remarkable.

explain: '~을 위해 ~을 희생하다'처럼 포기하는 것과 위하는 대상을 같이 말해요. 자기가 선택해서 내놓는다는 점이 '희생되다'와 달라요. 부모님, 가족 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Say what is given up and who it is for, as in '~을 위해 ~을 희생하다'. Unlike '희생되다', the person chooses to give it up. It suits talk about parents and family.

examples.en: I watched a baseball game in a dome.

examples.ko: 돔 안에서는 비가 와도 경기를 해요.
examples.en: Inside the dome, games go on even when it rains.
This city's dome is also used as a concert hall.

examples.ko: 돔의 지붕이 열리는 모습을 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the dome's roof open for the first time.
In autumn, I go to the dome to see concerts.
When the dome is closed, sound echoes loudly.

explain: 영어 dome에서 온 외래어예요. 한국에서는 '고척스카이돔'처럼 지붕이 있는 경기장 이름에 나와요. 지붕이 있는 야구장을 '돔구장'이라고도 불러요.
explain_en: It is a loanword from the English 'dome'. In Korea it appears in the names of roofed stadiums such as '고척스카이돔'. A baseball park with a roof is also called '돔구장'.

en: announce in advance; give advance notice

examples.ko: 방송에서 다음 주 눈 소식을 예고했어요.
examples.en: The broadcast gave advance notice of snow next week.
The teacher announced the test in advance.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 새 이야기를 예고하며 끝나요.
examples.en: That movie ends by hinting at a new story.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 신곡 발표를 예고하고 있어요.
examples.en: This singer is teasing the release of a new song.

examples.ko: 한 달 전에는 꼭 예고해 주세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to give notice a month ahead.
As announced, prices go up from today.

explain: '알리다'와 달리 일이 일어나기 전에 미리 알릴 때 써요. 영화 예고편, '태풍 예고', '파업 예고'처럼 앞으로 있을 일에 써요. 예고 없이 일어난 일은 '예고 없이'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '알리다', it is used for letting people know before something happens, as in a movie trailer (예고편) or '태풍 예고'. It is for things still to come. Something that happens without warning is '예고 없이'.

examples.ko: 정말 죄송해요. 한 번만 용서해 주세요.
examples.en: I'm really sorry. Please forgive me just once.
My friend apologized, so I forgave him right away.
It's not easy to forgive a lie.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 용서할 마음이 아직 없어요.
examples.en: I'm not yet ready to forgive that person.
After forgiving, my heart felt at ease.
Forgiving also takes courage.

explain: '용서하다'는 잘못을 무겁게 받아들이고 마음으로 풀어 주는 느낌이에요. 가벼운 실수에는 '괜찮아요'가 자연스러워요. '봐주다'는 이번만 넘어갈 때 써서 '용서하다'보다 가벼워요.
explain_en: '용서하다' feels weighty: taking a wrong seriously and letting it go in your heart. For small mistakes, '괜찮아요' is natural. '봐주다' means letting something slide this once and is lighter than '용서하다'.

examples.en: I called, but nobody answered.
Thank you for responding to the survey.
The customer center responded within ten minutes.
I like companies that respond to questions quickly.

examples.ko: 설문에 응답한 사람은 모두 이백 명이에요.
examples.en: Two hundred people responded to the survey in all.
To reply to an email, you must read it first.

explain: '대답하다'는 사람의 말에 직접 답할 때 쓰고, '응답하다'는 설문, 전화, 이메일, 서버처럼 요청이나 부름에 반응할 때 써요. 친구가 말을 걸 때는 '대답해요'가 자연스러워요. 컴퓨터가 멈추면 '응답 없음'이라고 떠요.
explain_en: '대답하다' is for answering what someone says directly; '응답하다' is for reacting to a request or call, such as a survey, phone call, email, or server. When a friend speaks to you, '대답해요' is natural. A frozen computer shows '응답 없음'.

examples.en: Please play this song again.
I played the video at double speed.
The sound cut out while it was playing.

examples.ko: 파일이 열리지 않아서 재생할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The file won't open, so I can't play it.
They recycle discarded bottles to make bags.
Regenerating skin takes time.

explain: 영상이나 음악 앱의 재생 버튼은 '재생'이라고 해요. 같은 말이 쓴 것을 다시 쓸 수 있게 만든다는 뜻이나 몸이 새로 생겨난다는 뜻으로도 쓰여서 문장을 보고 구분해야 해요. 멈출 때는 '일시정지'라고 해요.
explain_en: The play button in video and music apps is labeled '재생'. The same word is also used for making used things usable again and for the body growing back tissue, so tell them apart from the sentence. Pausing is '일시정지'.

examples.en: The photo was sent to my friend.
The file hasn't been sent yet.
Once the application is sent, an email arrives.
A message that has been sent can't be canceled.
The internet is slow, so the video transfers slowly.
All the data is being transmitted safely.

explain: 보내는 사람이 주어이면 '전송하다', 보낸 자료가 주어이면 '전송되다'예요. 사진, 파일, 메시지, 데이터를 보낼 때 써요. 택배는 '배송되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: When the sender is the subject use '전송하다'; when the sent item is the subject use '전송되다'. It is for photos, files, messages, and data. A parcel is '배송되다'.

examples.en: I'll pay for this meal by card.
I pay the rent at the end of every month.
I paid the price and got a receipt.
Please tell me how much I have to pay.

examples.ko: 이미 지불한 돈은 돌려받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: Money already paid can't be refunded.

examples.ko: 현금으로 지불하면 오백 원 깎아 줘요.
examples.en: If you pay in cash, they take off five hundred won.

explain: '내다'보다 딱딱한 말이고, '계산하다'가 계산대에서 값을 치르는 상황인 데 비해 '지불하다'는 돈을 건네는 일 자체를 말해요. 서류나 안내문에 '지불'이 보여요. 비슷한 '지급하다'는 월급이나 보험금처럼 받을 사람에게 돈을 내줄 때 써요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '내다'. Where '계산하다' is about settling the bill at the register, '지불하다' is about handing over the money itself, and '지불' shows up on forms and notices. The similar '지급하다' is for paying out money someone is owed, such as wages or insurance.

examples.en: Before the law, all people are equal.

examples.ko: 남자와 여자는 평등한 대우를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Men and women should receive equal treatment.
I think married couples should be equal too.
Unequal rules create complaints.

examples.ko: 기회가 평등해서 누구나 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Opportunity is equal, so anyone can take the exam.
Please give every student an equal chance.

explain: '공평하다'는 나누는 방법이 치우치지 않았다는 쪽이고, '평등하다'는 사람의 권리나 지위가 같다는 느낌이에요. 그래서 '평등한 사회', '남녀 평등'처럼 사람과 사회 이야기에 써요. 반대말은 '불평등하다'예요.
explain_en: '공평하다' is about sharing without bias, while '평등하다' is about people having the same rights or standing. So it is used for people and society, as in '평등한 사회' and '남녀 평등'. The opposite is '불평등하다'.

examples.ko: 날씨가 갑자기 악화해서 비행기가 못 떠요.
examples.en: The weather suddenly worsened, so the plane can't take off.

examples.ko: 병이 악화하지 않도록 약을 꼭 드세요.
examples.en: Take your medicine so the illness doesn't get worse.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 점점 악화하고 있어요.
examples.en: Relations between the two countries are gradually worsening.

examples.ko: 건강이 악화한 뒤로 일을 쉬고 있어요.
examples.en: Since my health deteriorated, I've been taking a break from work.
If the situation gets worse, contact me right away.
Noise made my relationship with the neighbors worse.

explain: '병이 악화하다', '관계가 악화하다'처럼 주어가 스스로 나빠질 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '악화되다'도 쓰고, 누군가 나빠지게 만들 때는 '악화시키다'를 써요. 반대말은 '호전되다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when the subject itself gets worse, as in '병이 악화하다' and '관계가 악화하다'. '악화되다' is also used with the same meaning, and '악화시키다' is for someone making things worse. The opposite is '호전되다'.

en: be wrapped; be gift-wrapped; be packed

examples.en: The gift has been wrapped prettily.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 한 개씩 포장돼 있어요.
examples.en: These snacks are packed one by one.

examples.ko: 포장된 음식은 집에서 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Packed food can be eaten at home.
If you order, it arrives safely packed in a box.

examples.ko: 길이 새로 포장되면 차가 편하게 다녀요.
examples.en: Once the road is newly paved, cars can travel comfortably.

examples.ko: 포장되지 않은 길은 비 오면 위험해요.
examples.en: An unpaved road is dangerous when it rains.

explain: 물건이 상자나 종이에 싸인 상태를 말해요. 식당에서 음식을 싸 갈 때 '포장해 주세요'는 사람이 하는 일이라 '포장하다'를 써요. '포장되다'는 길에 아스팔트를 깔았다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes an item being wrapped in a box or paper. When you ask a restaurant '포장해 주세요', a person does the action, so '포장하다' is used. '포장되다' is also used for a road that has been paved.

examples.en: I dried the wet clothes in the sun.
If you dry laundry in a dryer, it dries fast.
Mushrooms are dried and stored for a long time.
Dry your hair completely before you go out.
I like snacks made of dried fruit.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 공기를 건조시키는 기능이 있어요.
examples.en: This machine has a function that dries the air.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 보통 '말리다'를 써요. '건조시키다'는 기계, 식품, 공장 이야기처럼 딱딱한 설명에 어울려요. '날씨가 건조하다'는 형용사 '건조하다'라서 달라요.
explain_en: In everyday talk, '말리다' is the usual word. '건조시키다' suits stiff explanations about machines, food, and factories. '날씨가 건조하다' uses the adjective '건조하다', which is a different word.

examples.en: Your application is being reviewed now.
That plan has been reviewed several times.
I'll tell you tomorrow what was reviewed.
It has to be checked thoroughly for problems.
Once the new policy is reviewed, we'll announce it.

examples.ko: 그 안은 비용 때문에 검토되지 않았어요.
examples.en: That proposal wasn't considered because of the cost.

explain: 검토하는 사람이 아니라 검토를 받는 서류·계획·안건이 주어예요. '지금 검토 중이에요'라고도 말해요. 회사나 관공서에서 '검토 후 연락드리겠습니다'처럼 쓰는 말과 이어져요.
explain_en: The subject is the document, plan, or agenda item being reviewed, not the reviewer. You can also say '지금 검토 중이에요'. It connects to phrases used at companies and offices, such as '검토 후 연락드리겠습니다'.

examples.en: The criminal abandoned the car and fled.

examples.ko: 도둑이 담을 넘어 도망하는 모습이 카메라에 찍혔어요.
examples.en: The camera caught the thief climbing over the wall and fleeing.
Don't run away from difficult things.
The teacher found the student who had run off and hidden.
I saw news that the escaped animal had been found.
They say that person fled abroad.

explain: '도망가다', '도망치다', '달아나다'와 뜻이 비슷해요. '일에서 도망하다'처럼 어려운 일이나 책임을 피할 때도 써요. 벗어나려는 곳에는 '에서'를 붙여요.
explain_en: It is similar in meaning to '도망가다', '도망치다', and '달아나다'. It is also used for dodging hard work or responsibility, as in '일에서 도망하다'. The place you get away from takes '에서'.

examples.ko: 저는 새 지식으로 무장하고 면접에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the interview armed with new knowledge.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 우산과 장화로 무장해요.
examples.en: On rainy days I arm myself with an umbrella and boots.
In winter I bundled up completely in thick clothes.
A player armed with confidence stepped out.

examples.ko: 새로운 기술로 무장하면 취업이 더 쉬워져요.
examples.en: If you equip yourself with new skills, finding a job gets easier.

examples.ko: 무장하지 않은 시민들은 안전한 곳으로 피했어요.
examples.en: Unarmed citizens took refuge in a safe place.

explain: 원래는 무기를 갖춘다는 군대 이야기에 쓰는 말이에요. 요즘은 지식·기술·자신감 같은 것으로 단단히 준비한다는 비유로도 써요. '~으로 무장하다'처럼 '으로'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: Originally it belongs to military talk about being equipped with weapons. It is also used figuratively for getting solidly prepared with knowledge, skills, or confidence. It goes with '으로', as in '~으로 무장하다'.

examples.en: This magazine is published every month.

examples.ko: 새 책이 다음 주에 발행될 거예요.
examples.en: The new book will be published next week.

examples.ko: 표는 결제한 뒤에 바로 발행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Tickets are issued right after payment.
I read a newspaper that was published long ago.
So far one million copies have been printed.

examples.ko: 기념 우표가 발행되면 우체국에 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: When a commemorative stamp is issued, the line at the post office gets long.

explain: 책, 신문, 잡지, 영수증, 표, 우표 모두 '발행되다'와 쓸 수 있어요. 책은 '출판되다', '출간되다'도 쓰는데, 영수증이나 표처럼 만들어 내주는 것에는 '발행되다'가 어울려요.
explain_en: Books, newspapers, magazines, receipts, tickets, and stamps can all be '발행되다'. Books also use '출판되다' and '출간되다', but for things that are produced and handed out, like receipts and tickets, '발행되다' fits.
